newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Yapi Kredi Bank sells more shares abroad.
newsitem.headline: Turk Yapi Kredi Bank sells more shares abroad.

text.p: Yapi ve Kredi Bankasi AS (YKB), one of Turkey's leading commercial banks, said it sold an additional 708.87 million shares abroad on July 9, after selling 4,725.81 million shares via an international consortium on June 23.

"As a result of the consortium exercising its option to meet excess demand, the... additional Yapi Kredi Bank shares were sold at 3,100 lira per share, according to the June 23 sale agreement," YKB said in a statement.
It said YKB shareholders Cukurova Holding sold 190 million lira and Sinai ve Mali Yatirimlar Holding sold 518.87 million YKB shares, representing 1.17 percent of the bank's capital.

YKB sold 4,725.81 million shares, representing 7.87 percent of its capital, to 59 institutional investors abroad on June 23 via a consortium including Credit Suisse First Boston, Baring Brothers, Merrill Lynch Int, UBS Ltd and Swiss Bank Corp.
The June 23 sale of the YKB shares was made in the form of GDRs to be listed on the London stock Exchange and be traded as SEAC in London and PORTAL in the U.S.

YKB shares closed 350 lira higher at 3,950 lira on the national market on Thursday when the market index rallied 2.46 percent to a new all-time high close of 1,999. The bank's capital stands at 60.066 trillion lira.
